Examining a transverse section through the middle of the vaginate lamina (leaf pocket). The leaf midrib contains two peripheral guide cells (large, thin-walled) and two lateral bands of sterid cells (small, thick-walled) separated by one (sometimes more) large central cell.

Examining a transverse section through the middle of the vaginate lamina (leaf pocket). The leaf midrib contains three lateral bands (two lateral and one ventral) of sterid cells (small, thick-walled) and as many as 16 guide cells (large, thin-walled) arranged in a U or V formation, and as many as 5 large central cells.

Examining a transverse section through the middle of the vaginate lamina (leaf pocket). The leaf midrib contains four or more peripheral guide cells (large, thin-walled) and two lateral bands of sterid cells (small, thick-walled) separated by 1-5 large central cells.
